Description: Susceptible humans become exposed to the Zika virus through bites from infectious mosquitoes.
Exposed humans progress to the infectious stage after the incubation period.
Infectious humans recover from the Zika virus infection.
Mosquito eggs develop and hatch into the larval stage.
Mosquito larvae mature and transition into the pupal stage.
Mosquito pupae emerge as susceptible adult female mosquitoes.
Susceptible female mosquitoes become exposed to the Zika virus by biting infectious humans.
Exposed female mosquitoes become infectious after the virus incubation period.

Name: β
Description: The percentage of bites that transmit ZIKV.

Name: αH
Description: The inverse incubation time of ZIKV for human.

Name: γ
Description: The recovery rate of an infectious individual.

Name: λ
Description: The human population growth rate.

Name: αV
Description: The inverse incubation time of ZIKV in vectors.

Name: τi
Description: The reciprocal of the development time of vectors in stage i, where i ∈ {1, 2, 3} for egg, larvae, and pupae.

Name: μi
Description: The mortality rate of vectors in stage i, where i ∈ {1, 2, 3} for egg, larvae, and pupae.

Name: μV
Description: The mortality rate of adult vectors.

Name: KV
Description: Carrying capacity for larvae population.

Name: κ
Description: Mortality rate of larvae caused by limited carrying capacity.

Name: βb
Description: Number of infectious bites delivered per vector per day.

Name: 1/αH
Description: Incubation time in human.
